summary: AI observability tools provide visibility into how LLM applications behave in production, tracking traces, latency, token usage, costs, and output quality so teams can debug issues and control spending. As LLM apps scale, observability becomes essential for catching regressions, evaluating response quality, and preventing runaway API bills. The right tool combines distributed tracing, evaluation, and cost monitoring in one workflow.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, token usage, latency, cost, evaluation metrics, and prompt performance for LLM and agent applications.
features: Native integration with LangChain and LangGraph
tools.pricing: Free tier includes 5,000 monthly traces; Plus plan adds paid usage with base traces (14-day retention) at $2.50 per 1k and extended traces (400-day retention) at $5.00 per 1k; custom Enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams building with LangChain/LangGraph who want deeply integrated tracing and evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API requests, token usage, costs, latency, caching efficiency, and model performance via a lightweight proxy.
features: Cost and usage analytics per user or model
tools.pricing: Free tier includes 10,000 monthly traces; Pro plan at $79/month (approx $79 per 100,000 traces); Team plan at $799/month; custom Enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting quick, provider-agnostic cost tracking and logging with minimal code changes.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiments, model training metrics, evaluations, and prompt performance through W&B Weave.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for personal use; paid Pro and team plans with usage-based pricing; custom Enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: ML teams needing unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability in one platform.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production LLM and ML performance, drift, data quality, embeddings, traces, and evaluation metrics.
features: LLM tracing via OpenInference and Phoenix
Open-source Phoenix option for local tracing
tools.pricing: Free open-source Phoenix; Arize AX offers a free tier with paid Pro and custom Enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade ML and LLM monitoring with drift and RAG analysis.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: Traces, spans, token usage, cost, latency, evaluations, and prompt versions for LLM applications.
tools.pricing: Free self-hosted (open source); cloud Hobby tier free; Core and Pro paid plans with usage-based pricing; custom Enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, self-hostable observability stack with full data control.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM traces, token usage, latency, and costs using OpenTelemetry-based standardized instrumentation.
features: Vendor-neutral, exports to any OTel backend
Traces for prompts, vector DBs, and agents
tools.pricing: Free and open source; hosted Traceloop platform offers free tier with paid and Enterprise plans.
tools.best_for: Teams standardizing on OpenTelemetry who want vendor-neutral LLM instrumentation.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar requests so identical prompts don't incur redundant API calls, dramatically reducing token spend on common queries.
Route tasks to the cheapest capable model, using smaller or distilled models for simple tasks and reserving flagship models for complex reasoning.
Optimize prompts and context by trimming unnecessary tokens, truncating long histories, and using concise system prompts to lower input token costs.
Set usage limits, budgets, and alerts, and continuously monitor per-user and per-feature cost dashboards to catch runaway spending early.
